claims.summary: Snag 1 (Delimiter Depth Overflow): MAX_EXACT_REFERENCE_DELIMITER_DEPTH=4 (report L151); nesting beyond 4 (e.g. [[[...]]]) 'might fail to correctly identify the context, leading to incorrect marker preservation or omission.'
claims.disposition: verified_existing; CONTRADICTION preserved. Context is set by exact_reference_delimiter_pair(before.first(), after.first()) -- the innermost pair adjacent to the marker (L215), always inspected -- so context holds regardless of depth. Only the delimiter_depth COUNT saturates at 4 via take(4) (L208-223); the marker is NOT dropped. Covered by control_marker_cleanup_bounds_deeper_delimiter_receipt_without_dropping_token (tests.rs L2253: 5 levels -> depth 4, kept). Widening MAX is Tier-5; not made.

claims.summary: Snag 2 (Multi-byte Character Slicing): first_word_after (report L89-96) slices text[end..]; if end falls mid multi-byte UTF-8 char this causes a runtime panic.
claims.disposition: verified_existing; CONTRADICTION preserved. first_word_after's ONLY caller is L66, passing self.end = occurrence.end = offset.saturating_add(token.len()) (L110); offset is always a char boundary and token is a whole matched marker, so end is ALWAYS a valid char boundary -- the panic cannot occur. Byte-index concern is real and locked by control_marker_scanner_advances_byte_exactly_across_multibyte_text (L2099) + marker->emoji->relation tests (L2747, L2766).
